content: Sumatran Fleabane, scientifically known as Conyza sumatrensis, is commonly found in areas such as waste grounds, railways, and disturbed soils. This plant is characterized by its distinctly hairy floral bracts, which differentiate it from species like Conyza canadensis and Conyza bilbaoana. Additionally, the hairs on the leaf margins of Conyza sumatrensis are bent forward, unlike the right-angled spreading hairs seen in C. canadensis. The plant typically flowers during the months of August and September, producing pappus hairs that are dirty white or rust-colored. Despite being an abundant alien species, it is not considered invasive in natural or semi-natural habitats. Originally native to the American continent, Conyza sumatrensis has been introduced to the United Kingdom, where it is classified as a weed. In some countries, this species has begun to develop resistance to herbicides. In Britain, Conyza sumatrensis is the second most abundant alien species of the genus Conyza, following C. canadensis. It is predominantly found in London and the southeastern regions of England. Beyond the UK, this species is also present in countries such as Japan, Malaysia, Taiwan, Sri Lanka, and Australia.
